To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel event-based visual flow algorithm that uses multi-scale plane fitting for robustness to the aperture problem.
we present a novel multi-scale event-based visual flow estimation algorithm that is robust against the aperture problem and is fast and efficient.
we have proposed a new multi-scale event based visual flow method that is robust to aperture problem and can be used for predicting motion in real time.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) How to estimate motion direction of objects in the presence of aperture problem using dynamic vision sensors? (2) How to estimate flow direction of objects in a real world scenario using dynamic vision sensors and (3) How to use the estimated flow direction to make predictions of future events.
real-time event-driven visual flow estimation and prediction of motion for dynamic vision sensors.
the development and implementation of a robust, fast, and accurate event-based visual flow algorithm for the dynamic vision sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method can perform real-time event-by-event visual flow and motion prediction using dynamic vision sensors.

our proposed algorithm is the first of its kind that is able to estimate motion in real time and is able to perform motion estimation event by event, thus allowing for predictions of motion up to 10 to even 25 frames ahead.
we present a novel multi-scale event-driven visual flow algorithm that overcomes the aperture problem and is computationally fast.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed algorithm can predict the next motion frame in real-time and is robust to the common problems of visual flow computation in dynamic sensors.
we have developed a fast and robust visual flow algorithm for dynamic vision sensors that allows for accurate motion prediction.
we have a fast and efficient visual flow algorithm that can predict motion of objects up to 500ms in advance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we demonstrate the ability to estimate motion in a real world scenario using only the sparse and precise temporal information of the events and that this is sufficient for real-time predictions.
the dynamic vision sensors are very suitable for real time applications that require high frame rates and precise temporal resolution.
the dynamic sensors can be used for motion prediction and can provide an additional cue to the visual processing system.
